question.text: Narmada Buyout Fund II (Category II AIF) is nearing its 7-year stated tenure with two portfolio companies still un-exited. The Manager proposes to extend the fund tenure by 2 years. What approval threshold and process applies?

answer.text: Approval of two-thirds of unit-holders by value of their investment; no SEBI approval required
Simple majority of unit-holders and prior SEBI approval
Unanimous consent of all investors and Trustees
Sponsor's unilateral discretion up to the extension cap

explanation.text: The Logic: Extension of tenure of close-ended Cat I/II AIFs is permitted up to 2 years, subject to approval of two-thirds (66.67%) of unit-holders by value of their investment in the AIF. No separate SEBI approval is mandated. If the required 2/3 consent is not obtained, the AIF must fully liquidate within 1 year following tenure expiry. LVFs/AI-only Funds may extend up to 5 years on the same 2/3 basis. The Trap: Option B's 'simple majority + SEBI approval' conflates with material PPM changes. Option C's 'unanimous' is over-restrictive. Option D's 'Sponsor unilateral' violates governance norms. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this identically. XIX-A Distributors should understand extension mechanics when LP client wants exit clarity. In Mutual Funds (NISM V-A), scheme tenure is not comparable — open-ended schemes have no tenure. The 2/3 value-based voting is unique to the AIF unit-holder framework. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build the extension playbook early: (i) send LP notice 12 months before original tenure end, (ii) host an advisory-committee call detailing exit pipeline, (iii) run the vote at least 6 months before the expiry. If you fail 2/3, the forced-liquidation-within-1-year creates massive distressed exit pressure.
